pr_body:
Fixes #4092 

I tried to follow all the directions in `CONTRIBUTING` but this is my first PR here, apologies in advance if something is off.
I used and re-adjusted the tests from `last()` because it seemed to have a larger coverage.

I have two items I'm not too sure about though:
- `IgnoreNulls()` inside `FirstState`, I'm not sure if it's useful to add a param to the template and return that. I did it for `FirstVectorFunction` but it seemed more natural there
- About the comparison with BigQuery, the behavior is a bit different when it comes to arrays because for BigQuery `NULL` is basically `[NULL]` but not for DuckDB. The current change considers only `NULL` and not `[NULL]` as something to skip. 

There is still the issue mentioned in #4092 about `UNION ALL` blocks but I guess that applies to `last()` so maybe it could be another issue / PR ?
pr_comments: Could you also have a look at the vector sizes test that is failing? You can test this failure locally by changing `STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE` in `vector_size.hpp` to 2 and re-compiling.

(please let me know if Discord is a better place for these discussion)

About the vector size test failing, I can reproduce locally setting `STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE` to 2 but I'm not totally sure I understand the failure (btw I think `skewness()` and `kurtosis()` and some others fail too with this small vector size, their tests have a `require vector_size 512`).

I get where the failure comes from and it does work mapping `"any_value"` in `transform_function.cpp` but I have a couple doubts:
- why does `any_value()` work fine with larger (default) `STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE`. I'm assuming this is intended but I'm not sure I understand why. The type of window functions explicitly defined as `WINDOW_*` is a small set vs the regular aggregate functions, does it mean they all would have the same behavior? From the change of `vector_size` in the `*.test` I guess so
- on how to solve this, should `any_value` become a new `ExpressionType`, i.e. `WINDOW_ANY_VALUE`? Asking since `any_value()` in window function is basically `first(... ignore nulls)`, so not sure if I should try to somewhat overload `WINDOW_FIRST_VALUE`. 

Or maybe to align with the other functions, should I just use `require vector_size 512` in the tst like some other aggregate functions do?

Window functions in general do not work with vector sizes of 2 currently because of the way the window segment tree is setup. That is unrelated to this PR and applies to all window function aggregates, as you have noticed as well. All you need to do is add `require vector_size 512` to the test.

The `WINDOW_` aggregates are special aggregates that only exist for window functions - all regular aggregates automatically work with window functions as well. Nothing is required to get that to work aside from implementing our aggregate function interface.

Thanks! 

I'm not sure about the two tests that still fail, I think "CodeQuality" used to pass and from the log I'm not sure if it was transitory or not, I can't seem to be able to restart it myself
Looks like they were spurious failures. Thanks for the PR!

issue_context.title: Support ANY_VALUE aggregate function
issue_context.body: Google BigQuery supports the [any_value](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#any_value) aggregate function which returns the first non-null value encountered. We have a similar function (`first`), but it returns the first value encountered. We would like to add support for the `ANY_VALUE` function as well.
comments:
I'd like to give it a shot, unless somebody picked it already.

I went through the code but I've a few questions:
1. I think this could be implemented either in `first.cpp` adding an extra template parameter and tweaking the logic or adding a new class altogether (e.g. `any_value.cpp`), what's the preferred approach?
2. When trying to run tests via `make unit` (from CONTRIBUTING) they take a lot longer than a minute, more around 15-20min, is that expected? I'm talking about running the tests, not building them. Am I doing something wrong?
3. When looking into the existing code I noticed `last()` always returns the value from the first query block in case of union all (e.g. `select last(n) from (select 0 n union all select 1)` (reproduces in shell.duckdb.org), is that expected behavior? If not maybe I could try to look into that too (unless you think it would get too hard as a first issue) 

Full disclosure: my C++ is very rusty so I may stumble on simple things, apologies in advance

Hey, awesome to hear you wanna pick this up 1. I haven't looked into it too much, but it sounds like `first` could have an optional second parameter, that - when passed a certain value like `SKIP_NULLS` for example - will make `first` skip null values.
Then `ANY_VALUE` could be a macro that calls `first` with `SKIP_NULLS`. (have a look at `src/catalog/default/default_functions.cpp` to see what I mean by macro) 2. I believe `make unit` runs all (fast) unit tests, as that is the default behavior of `build/debug/test/unittest`. But this same binary can also run a specific test file, which is useful for debugging, for example: `./unittest test/sql/aggregate/aggregates/test_first_noninlined.test` I can't really give you an answer on 3 though, hopefully Mytherin has an answer for you :)
